subject.title: Session `status` field values ("failed", "timeout", "done") mislead agents into spawning duplicate sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose a backward-compatible `resumable` or status-semantics signal for `sessions_list`, and should that signal live in the shared Gateway row or only in the agent-facing tool projection?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but changing model-visible session state can alter routing behavior for `done`, `failed`, `timeout`, `killed`, and future statuses, so automation should not choose the permanent API contract alone.

options.title: Add agent-facing resumability guidance
options.body: Keep the shipped status values and add a clear `resumable`/status-semantics hint in the agent `sessions_list` output and prompt text, limiting Gateway/client API expansion unless explicitly needed.

options.title: Promote `resumable` to Gateway row contract
options.body: Add `resumable` to shared Gateway session rows too, with tests and client compatibility review for Control UI and protocol consumers.

options.title: Redesign lifecycle statuses
options.body: Pause the additive fix and define separate turn-state versus lifecycle-state fields or renamed statuses, accepting a larger compatibility and migration discussion.

recommendation.title: Add agent-facing resumability guidance
recommendation.body: Keep the shipped status values and add a clear `resumable`/status-semantics hint in the agent `sessions_list` output and prompt text, limiting Gateway/client API expansion unless explicitly needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-row work plus broad session/tool ownership makes this the best available owner for the product/API contract choice.
